title: Stack Trace Reconstructor
summary: Reconstruct exclusive function runtimes from nested start/end profiler events.

testCases.name: computes exclusive time for nested calls
testCases.input:
logs = [
    "0 root start",
    "2 parse start",
    "5 parse end",
    "6 fetch start",
    "9 fetch end",
    "10 root end",
]
exclusive_time(logs)

testCases.name: aggregates repeated calls
testCases.input:
logs = [
    "0 main start",
    "1 helper start",
    "3 helper end",
    "4 helper start",
    "7 helper end",
    "8 main end",
]
exclusive_time(logs)

testCases.name: rejects mismatched stack endings
code: for logs in (["0 a start", "1 b end"], ["0 a end"]):

testCases.name: handles sequential non nested calls
setup: logs = ["0 load start", "3 load end", "3 save start", "5 save end"]
testCases.input:
logs = ["0 load start", "3 load end", "3 save start", "5 save end"]
exclusive_time(logs)

testCases.name: rejects unknown events
code: exclusive_time(["0 main start", "1 main pause", "2 main end"])

testCases.name: empty trace has no runtime totals
keeps zero duration calls in the result
parent resumes after a zero duration child
testCases.input: exclusive_time(["0 root start", "2 child start", "2 child end", "5 root end"])

testCases.name: aggregates recursive frames without counting idle gaps
testCases.input: exclusive_time(["0 work start", "2 work start", "5 work end", "7 work end", "20 work start", "21 work end"])

clarifyingQuestions: Are end timestamps inclusive or exclusive?
Can functions recurse or appear more than once in the stream?
Should invalid nesting raise, skip, or return partial results?
followUps: Return a call tree alongside the aggregate exclusive-time totals.
Track top functions by exclusive runtime.
Handle streaming logs where a call can remain open across batches.
followUpGuide: For a call tree, push a frame object with name, start time, child time, and children. On `end`, compute total time and exclusive time, then attach the frame to its parent.
For top functions, keep the same `totals` dictionary and sort by `(-runtime, name)` at the end. Clarify whether ties should be deterministic.

For streaming input, retain the stack and last timestamp across batches and validate unclosed calls only at an explicit finish(). Decide whether each batch returns runtime deltas or cumulative totals; summing cumulative snapshots would double count. Idle time after a completed top-level call remains unattributed.
complexityAnalysis: - Stack guide: O(n) event operations for n logs, with O(d + f) records including output totals, where d is maximum nesting depth and f is the distinct function count. Reading/splitting/hashing strings adds O(L) character work for L total input characters; integer arithmetic is treated as constant cost. Peak parsing space also includes the longest line.

- Per-frame alternative: store each call's start time and accumulated child duration. At end, exclusive time is end - start - child_duration; add its full duration to the parent's child_duration. The same stack gives O(n) event operations and O(d + f) space without storing a complete tree.

- Call-tree follow-up retains one node per invocation, so space can grow to O(n). Ranking f totals costs O(f log f) comparisons. Sorting the input isn't needed and mustn't reorder events at equal timestamps.
solutionGuide: Use an explicit stack of active function names. Keep `last_ts`, the timestamp where the currently active frame started accumulating time.
Before every event, add `timestamp - last_ts` to the function on top of the stack. Then process the event. This keeps parent time exclusive because children take over the active slot.
if last_ts is not None and stack:
if not stack or stack[-1] != name:

The invariant is that last_ts marks the beginning of the next interval to attribute. Only stack[-1] earns that interval; an empty stack means idle time. A recursive child has the same name as its parent but still occupies a separate stack slot, so its interval is added once to that name's total. Complexity is O(n) event operations and O(d + f) stored records, plus the character/parsing costs described above.
